$comment: D4.26 — THE MISSING SAME-AXIS INTERACTION RULE, AND WHY IT WAS NOT PORTED.
D4.25 established that a liability cap and an indemnity can jointly promise more cover than
the cap permits, that the guarantee family prevents this with an express interaction sentence,
and that five families carrying both decision-bearing clauses have no such sentence.
The instruction was to extract the SEMANTIC CONTRACT of the guarantee wording rather than copy
the sentence, and to create one reusable treatment ONLY IF the semantics are genuinely identical
across the affected families.
THEY ARE NOT, AND THE EVIDENCE IS MECHANICAL RATHER THAN A MATTER OF JUDGEMENT.
The shipped cap in all five families reads: 'shall not exceed the total consideration paid under
this Agreement'. NDA and FOUNDERS_AGREEMENT COLLECT NO CONSIDERATION FIELD AT ALL — no fee, no
amount, no price, nothing the phrase can measure. In an NDA the consideration is frequently nil
or nominal by design. So porting the guarantee's 'the indemnity forms part of, and shall not
increase, the aggregate cap' into an NDA would fold a mutual confidentiality indemnity into a cap
of nothing, and extinguish it.
That is the opposite of what the guarantee sentence does there, where the cap is a stated rupee
figure and folding the indemnity into it is a real limit rather than an erasure. Same words,
opposite effect. The condition for a single reusable treatment therefore fails, and nothing was
attached to any family.
WHAT IS RECORDED INSTEAD: the interaction as an UNDECIDED decision with three candidate
directions, per-family analysis of which is likely intended, and the authority for each. An
advocate decides; this file states the question and what turns on it.

what_the_guarantee_asserts: CAP: the ceiling applies to guarantee liability AND indemnity liability taken together.
INDEMNITY: liability under it forms part of the cap and does not increase it.
Stripped of its wording, the relationship is: TWO PROVISIONS QUANTIFY THE SAME EXPOSURE, AND
ONE IS DECLARED TO BE CONSUMED BY THE OTHER'S CEILING. The direction is what matters, and the
guarantee happens to choose one of three available directions.
semantic_contract.the_general_relation: SAME_AXIS_INTERACTION — two treatments quantify one exposure, and the instrument must say which bounds which, or neither does.

candidate_directions.reading: Indemnity liability counts toward the aggregate cap and cannot exceed it.
candidate_directions.used_by: GUARANTEE_AGREEMENT, expressly and from both ends
candidate_directions.appropriate_where: The cap is a stated figure and the indemnity is a payment obligation of the same order — a guarantor's exposure, a supplier's service liability.
candidate_directions.destroys_the_indemnity_where: The cap has no measurable referent or is nil, which is exactly the NDA and FOUNDERS_AGREEMENT position.

candidate_directions.reading: The indemnity is carved out; the cap does not limit it.
candidate_directions.appropriate_where: The indemnified harm is unquantifiable or falls on third parties — confidentiality breach, IP infringement, personal injury on demised premises. Market practice in NDAs and leases treats these as uncapped heads.

authority.note: A sum named in the contract is recoverable as reasonable compensation, not automatically in full — so an uncapped indemnity is not an unlimited one in practice.
Compensation for loss naturally arising, which is what an uncapped indemnity leaves the court to measure.

candidate_directions.reading: Specified heads sit outside the cap; the rest are inside it.
candidate_directions.appropriate_where: The cap already carves out fraud and wilful misconduct, so the instrument is ALREADY doing this in part. The open question is whether breach and negligence — both indemnity triggers — belong inside or outside.
note: This is the most interesting candidate because the shipped cap already reads 'except in cases
of fraud, wilful misconduct, or liabilities that cannot be limited under applicable law', while
the indemnity triggers on 'breach of this Agreement, negligence, or wilful misconduct'.
Wilful misconduct is therefore already outside the cap and already an indemnity trigger — the
two clauses ALREADY interact, coherently, on one of three heads. Breach and negligence are the
heads where nothing has been said.

per_family.cap_measure: total consideration paid under this Agreement
per_family.why: An NDA frequently has no consideration beyond mutual promises, so a cap measured on consideration paid is nil or unstatable. Folding a confidentiality indemnity into it would leave the disclosing party with a remedy of nothing, which cannot be what either party intends by signing a confidentiality agreement.
per_family.verdict: PORTING THE GUARANTEE PATTERN HERE WOULD BE A SUBSTANTIVE HARM, NOT A CLARIFICATION.

per_family.cap_measure: total consideration paid under this Agreement
per_family.why: Founders typically pay each other nothing under the founders' agreement itself; value moves through the company. The cap has no referent, and whether the indemnity should be limited at all is a question about the founders' bargain rather than about drafting hygiene.
per_family.verdict: The cap's measure is the prior defect. The interaction question cannot be answered until it is.

per_family.cap_measure: total consideration paid under this Agreement
per_family.why: Rent paid to date is a measurable figure that grows over the term, so the cap means something. But a lease indemnity commonly answers third-party claims — injury on the premises, statutory liability — and capping those at rent paid would leave the landlord or tenant exposed to a claim the instrument purports to allocate.
per_family.verdict: Plausible but not obvious. Needs the advocate to separate third-party heads from inter-party heads.

per_family.cap_measure: total consideration paid under this Agreement
per_family.why: Same analysis as the commercial lease; the licence fee supplies a measurable cap.
per_family.verdict: Resolves with COMMERCIAL_LEASE_AGREEMENT as one question, not two.

per_family.cap_measure: total consideration paid under this Agreement
per_family.why: The clause is mutual — 'each Party shall indemnify the other' — but the two directions are not symmetrical in employment. An employee's indemnity to the employer capped at salary paid may be generous to the employer; an employer's indemnity to the employee capped at the same figure may be inadequate. Employment law constrains what an employer may recover from an employee in ways this clause does not acknowledge.
per_family.verdict: The mutuality is the defect here, not the cap. Not N-party admissible, so it is outside the scope this phase was scoped to.

what_was_deliberately_not_done: No clause text was changed in any family.
No single interaction treatment was attached, because the semantics are not identical and the
instruction made identity the condition for a reusable shape.
No cross-treatment consistency engine was built — D4.25 falsified that hypothesis and D4.26
LIABILITY_CAP_APPORTIONMENT REMAINS OPEN AND UNTOUCHED. Ordering the indemnity against the cap
says nothing about whether the cap is per-party, shared, or inter se once there are three
principals. The two questions compose and must not be allowed to resolve each other by
accident: an interaction treatment that silently assumed a shared cap would answer an open
legal question as a side effect of a drafting fix.

incidental_defect.finding: The cap measures 'the total consideration paid under this Agreement' in five families, two of which collect no consideration field of any kind.
incidental_defect.independent_of: the interaction question and the N-party question alike
incidental_defect.note: Worth repairing on its own terms. A ceiling that cannot be computed is not a limitation of liability; it is an unresolved reference that a court would have to fill.

blocking_prior.status: UNDECIDED — AND IT BLOCKS THE INTERACTION DECISION
hierarchy: ├── measurable   → the interaction decision may be meaningful
└── unmeasurable → the interaction decision is BLOCKED
why_it_blocks: Asking an advocate whether the indemnity consumes a ceiling that cannot be computed is asking
them to order a clause against a quantity that does not exist. The answer would be recorded, it
would look like progress, and it would mean nothing.
A ceiling that cannot be computed is not a limitation of liability. It is an unresolved
reference, and a court asked to apply it would have to supply the missing term or treat the
limitation as ineffective — the opposite of what the party relying on it expects.

two_distinct_failures.what: The form offers 'Fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim' as a cap basis and the family collects no fee of any kind. Partners and shareholders do not pay fees to one another under the deed, so the option is category-wrong for the family rather than merely unsupported.
two_distinct_failures.repair: An intake question, and an advocate's view on what these instruments should measure instead — capital contributed, shareholding, a stated sum, or no monetary cap.

two_distinct_failures.what: No cap-basis question at all, and the clause's fixed prose measures a quantity the family never collects. The user cannot configure it and the instrument cannot compute it.
two_distinct_failures.repair: The D4.26 case generalised. NDA and FOUNDERS_AGREEMENT were the two found by hand; there are six.

note: The four states are distinguished because they need different repairs. Conflating them into
'the cap is broken' would put an intake question and a drafting question in one queue item.

advocate_queue_item.title: CAP_MEASUREMENT / CONSIDERATION_REFERENCE
advocate_queue_item.question: For each family whose cap cannot be computed, what is the liability ceiling actually meant to measure, if anything: stated consideration or fees, a separately stated monetary amount, another contract-specific quantity, or no monetary cap at all?
advocate_queue_item.constraint: Subsequent indemnity-interaction decisions must not resolve or imply this question. An interaction treatment that assumed a measure would answer it as a side effect.

authority.note: Compensation for loss naturally arising. A cap displaces this measure, so a cap that cannot be computed displaces it with nothing.
A sum named in the contract is recoverable as reasonable compensation. A ceiling with no referent is not a named sum.

why: The shipped cap already carves out three heads while the indemnity triggers on three, and
they overlap on exactly one. So the instrument is ALREADY ordering the two clauses in part,
and a Boolean 'is the indemnity capped?' would overwrite a settled head to answer an open one.

heads.head: WILFUL_MISCONDUCT
heads.state: SETTLED — and it is the one head where the two clauses already interact coherently

interaction_is_per_head_not_boolean.consequence: The open question is two heads wide, not a whole clause wide. That is a materially cheaper thing to put to an advocate, and it is only visible because the clause text was read rather than summarised.

three_layers_must_not_contaminate: MEASUREMENT   — what does the ceiling measure? Blocks everything below it.
INTERACTION   — per head, does the indemnity consume that ceiling, sit outside it, or is it carved?
APPORTIONMENT — with N principals, is the ceiling per-party, shared, or inter se?
Each is a separate advocate decision with separate authority, and none may resolve another as a
side effect. The apportionment question is LIABILITY_CAP_APPORTIONMENT and remains open and
untouched; the interaction question is blocked wherever measurement is unresolved; measurement is

retracted_finding.claim: Ten document types collect a liability cap figure and state a different basis in the clause, so the user's number never reaches the page.
why: draftConsistencyValidator.js already reports it as LIABILITY_CAP_ANSWERS_CONFLICT. The user
also chose a BASIS, the clause follows the basis, and the validator says in terms that the
figure has not been used. Verified by generating three of the ten and reading the output.
Recorded because the retraction is the useful part: the probe was one step from reporting
correct, already-disclosed behaviour as a defect, and what stopped it was checking whether
the system already said so rather than treating silence as confirmation.
